spans.s:
Āṇḍīka (‘bearing eggs’) is a term found in the Atharvaveda denoting an edible plant, apparently with fruit or leaves of egg shape (āṇḍa), akin to the lotus.
Foot notes iv. 34, 5; v. 17, 16. In the first passage the Paippalāda version has pauṇḍarīka in its place; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 207. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 70; Weber, Indische Studien, 18, 138.
